— 🇮🇷 NEW: Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, issued a message on the occasion of Holy Defense Week and the martyrdom anniversary of Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah
In the message, the following important points were mentioned:
– The days when Western powers controlled Iran and imposed their will upon the Iranian nation are long gone; the Islamic Revolution has awakened the people’s spirits, and I assure the people those dark days will never be repeated.
– Controlling the Strait of Hormuz is a joint desire of the entire Iranian nation, despite the differences between some segments in society.
– Throughout the past few wars, starting with the first imposed war [Saddam’s invasion], Iran has risen from the ashes of war like a burning Phoenix, and has become so powerful that it now casts its shadow on the enemy’s lands. 
– Since the time of the Prophets, no greater figure than Sayyed Hassan Nasrallah has appeared in the land of Al-Sham [the Levant], and with his stature, wisdom and courageous actions he turned Lebanon into a jewel of the Resistance and brought it to a position of greatness.
– Some people these days consider Iran to be the 4th world superpower, but that is according to worldly calculations; when God is entered into the equation, Iran is a divine power, second to none.
– In some important areas of bravery and presence in the fields, women have outpaced men.
– Today, the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz have been emptied of American military presence, and their navy does not dare to advance beyond the Arabian Sea; God Willing, they will sooner or later be expelled from the Arabian Sea as well.

South Korea's defense agency approached Türkiye's TEI about buying PD170 drone engines after repeated failures of domestic military drones. 
At a September 16 defense drone expo, a KAI jet-powered UAV crashed immediately after takeoff. 
In August, two kamikaze drones launched from the navy's Marado ship both plunged into the sea within seconds. 
Meanwhile, the PD170 powers Türkiye's combat-proven Bayraktar TB2/TB3 and Anka/Aksungur drones, with Aksungur logging 45 hours endurance and 42,000 ft altitude.
South Korea's defense exports are booming (Chunmoo rockets, K2 tanks, Cheongung-II missiles) but the drone sector lags significantly behind.
Source: Yonhap

⚡️🇰🇵 North Korean state-linked hackers are again suspected of stealing $387.5 million from cryptocurrency, this time in Bitget, in what is being described as the largest crypto theft of 2026 so far.
Bitget CEO Chen said the attackers exploited an internal system to manipulate transaction approvals, while the exchange’s cold wallets remained unaffected. Bitget temporarily suspended withdrawals and plans to restore them in stages from September 28.
This follows the February 2025 $1.5 billion Bybit hack, which the FBI attributed to North Korean hackers, making it one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts ever recorded. North Korean hacking groups have been linked to major cryptocurrency thefts, with proceeds reportedly helping fund the country’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes according to US treasury Department.

🔥⚔️ New strikes in Kiev renew questions over Ukraine’s gaps in air defense
Kiev’s air defenses were questioned by Ukrainian MP Oleksiy Goncharenko after a drone struck the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in the city center.
He cited shortages of Patriot missiles and criticized the failure to intercept what he described as an ordinary Shahed-type drone, arguing that Kiev should focus on air defense rather than retaliatory strikes. He also claimed that the skies over the capital are effectively under Russian control and warned that the situation raises concerns ahead of winter.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko also reported a hit on a seven-story administrative building, while the Dobrobut medical center was damaged and caught fire.
What was hit in Kiev:
🌏 A building near Ukraine’s Constitutional Court

🌏 The Dobrobut medical center, which was heavily damaged and caught fire
Separately, authorities in Brovary in the Kiev region reported elevated ammonia levels near a warehouse hit in a strike and advised residents to keep windows closed and limit time outdoors.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🔥🇹🇷🇮🇱 Israel feels ‘threatened’ by Turkish-Libyan maritime pact
 
The 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime jurisdiction agreement delimited exclusive economic zones (EEZ) in the eastern Mediterranean favoring the two nations, preempting the Israel-Cyprus-Greece EastMed pipeline project before it could be implemented and assuring that no regional energy projects could bypass Turkey.
In 2020, Egypt and Greece signed their own maritime pact, setting up competing EEZs for oil and gas drilling rights cutting directly through the Turkish-Libyan-claimed corridor.
The IDF’s Intelligence Directorate has formally “begun focusing” on the Turkish-Libyan deal, as well as “Turkey’s growing military and diplomatic influence in the region,” defense sources told JPost. The sources highlighted Turkey’s growing presence in Libya’s ports and airspace, and exploration of energy resources in Libyan waters, in exchange for military assistance.
For Israel, a strengthened Turkey-Libya relationship gives Ankara the capacity to disrupt the “freedom of navigation” of Israeli commercial shipping, which accounts for 98% of the country’s imports, and is “particularly sensitive” amid the Houthi’s ability to target its vessels in the Red Sea.
Besides blocking EastMed, the ties are said to threaten Israel’s deployment of “undersea communications infrastructure and electricity cables in areas where there are clear concerns they could be damaged.”
👉The potential for maritime escalation comes amid broader tensions between [Israel and Turkey](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74192), with some Israeli politicians even openly saying a [hot war may](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71901) be in the offing.
